units.source_text: “这就跟衣领和袖口一样，与其用脏的，不如一开始就用带颜色的，要是用白的，就干脆用雪白的。”

en.t: “It is the same with collars and cuffs: rather than use dirty ones, it is better to use colored ones from the start; if you use white ones, then they ought to be pure white.”

units.source_text: 如此说来，先生的确有洁癖。

en.t: Put that way, Sensei certainly did have a fastidious streak.

units.source_text: 书房、客房总是收拾得整洁有序。

en.t: His study and guest room were always kept neat and orderly.

units.source_text: 我一向邋里邋遢，所以先生的这种特点，总能引起我的注意。

en.t: Since I have always been careless and untidy, this trait of Sensei's always caught my attention.

units.source_text: “先生有洁癖啊。”一次，我对夫人这样说时，

en.t: “Sensei is rather fastidious, isn't he?” I once said this to his wife,

units.source_text: 她曾回答：“可他对衣服就不那么讲究了。”

en.t: and she replied, “But he is not so particular about his clothes.”

units.source_text: 先生在一旁听了，笑着说：“说实在的，我精神上有洁癖，所以一直很苦恼，想来真是愚蠢的天性。”

en.t: Sensei, who had been listening nearby, laughed and said, “To tell the truth, I am fastidious in spirit, and that makes me suffer all the time; when I think about it, it is a truly foolish disposition.”

units.source_text: 我不知道先生说的精神上的洁癖，是指一般人所说的神经质，还是指理论上的洁癖。

en.t: I did not know whether the spiritual fastidiousness Sensei spoke of meant what people generally call nervousness, or whether he meant a fastidiousness of principle.
His wife could not explain it either.

units.source_text: 那晚，我同先生对坐在像往常一样洁白的桌布前。

en.t: That evening, Sensei and I sat facing each other before the tablecloth, white as usual.

units.source_text: 夫人把我们安置在餐桌左右两边，自己居中，坐在正对庭院的座位上。

en.t: His wife seated us on the left and right sides of the dining table, while she herself sat in the middle, in the seat facing the garden.

units.source_text: “祝贺你毕业。”说着，先生为我举起了酒杯。

en.t: “Congratulations on your graduation,” Sensei said, raising his cup for me.

units.source_text: 对于这杯酒，我并没有感到特别高兴。

en.t: I did not feel especially pleased by this cup of wine.

units.source_text: 原因之一是，我内心并没有一听到这话就欢喜雀跃般地兴奋，

en.t: One reason was that, in my own heart, I did not have the kind of leaping joy that would spring up at hearing those words,

units.source_text: 而且先生说这句话的口吻，也丝毫没有让我高兴的喜兴劲儿。

en.t: and Sensei's tone when he said them had none of the buoyant cheer that might have made me glad.

units.source_text: 先生笑着举起酒杯，我在他的笑容中，看不到半点儿恶意的讽刺，同时也感觉不到他说祝贺时的真情。

en.t: Sensei raised his cup with a smile; in that smile I could see not the slightest malicious irony, but neither could I feel any real warmth in his congratulations.

units.source_text: 先生的笑仿佛在告诉我：“一般在这种场合，总要说祝贺的呀。”

en.t: Sensei's smile seemed to be telling me, “In situations like this, people generally say congratulations.”
